intro.text: Gach Alley is only about 128 metres long, lined with small cafes and guesthouses, and midway along it stands a communal house with a stele dated 1430.

nodes.name: Thanh Ha Communal House
nodes.summary: A communal house for Tran Luu, holding a stele dated 1430 that the press calls the oldest surviving in Hanoi.
nodes.story: Halfway along Gach Alley a few steps lead to Thanh Ha communal house. The legend says Tran Luu took the command when the court officials all stepped back, defeated the invaders, feasted his troops, and vanished in a storm. That is a legend, not something we can verify. What still stands is a stele dated 1430, which the press calls the oldest surviving stele in Hanoi. A plaque at the gate marks it as a ranked monument.

nodes.name: Cau Dong Pagoda
nodes.summary: A pagoda just beyond the western end, also honouring the Grand Master Tran Thu Do and his wife.
nodes.story: Step out of the western end and you reach Cau Dong Pagoda. Its curiosity is a pair of wooden statues of Tran Thu Do and his wife. The pagoda says it has no records of where the statues came from. Some say Lady Tran Thi Dung once paid for repairs, but that is only a legend.
nodes.caption: Cau Dong Pagoda at 38B Hang Duong, just outside the western entrance of Gach Alley.
